card_text: Features, structure and lead generation for business and corporate websites.
title: Business & Corporate Website Development Services
h1: Business and corporate website development that generates leads
author: Hiten Neotia
excerpt: Business website development for small businesses and corporates: essential pages, features, lead generation and how to match the site to your business model.

faqs.q: Why does a small business need a professional website?
faqs.a: It builds credibility, makes you visible 24/7, brings in leads, helps you rank in local search and lets you compete with bigger brands.

faqs.q: How much does a small business website cost?
faqs.a: In India, a basic site often costs ₹15,000 to ₹50,000, and a business site with a CMS, SEO and integrations usually ₹30,000 to ₹3 lakh.

faqs.q: What features should a business website have?
faqs.a: Clear service pages, contact forms, WhatsApp and click-to-call, reviews, fast mobile pages, HTTPS, analytics and a CMS your team can update.

faqs.q: How does a website help with local SEO?
faqs.a: Location pages, consistent business details and a linked Google Business Profile help you appear in local and 'near me' searches.

faqs.q: What are common small business website mistakes?
faqs.a: No clear call to action, slow mobile pages, one vague services page, outdated content and no tracking of where leads come from.

content_html:
Business and corporate website development that generates leads

Business website development gives a company a credible home online that works around the clock. A good business website builds trust, shows up in local search, answers customer questions and turns visitors into enquiries. Small businesses need clear pages and easy contact options. Corporate sites add investor, careers and multi-team content on top.

Why every small business needs a professional website

Customers check a business online before they call or visit. A professional website gives you:

  • Credibility. A clean, current site signals a real, reliable business.
  • 24/7 visibility. People can find you and learn about you at any time.
  • Leads. Forms, WhatsApp buttons and click-to-call turn interest into enquiries.
  • Local SEO. Location pages and a linked Google Business Profile help you win “near me” searches.
  • A level playing field. A strong site lets a small business compete with bigger brands.

Business website development: the pages you need

In practice, most business websites need a home page, an about page, one page per service, case studies or testimonials, a contact page and legal pages. Add location pages if you serve several areas, and a blog if you want to rank for questions your customers ask. For that reason, one clear page per service ranks and converts far better than one long “services” page.

Essential corporate website features

  • Brand-consistent design and a clear structure for large amounts of content.
  • A CMS so several teams can update their own sections.
  • Multilingual content where you serve different markets.
  • Investor relations and careers sections.
  • Accessibility, HTTPS and a web application firewall.
  • Structured data so search engines and AI tools understand your organisation.

How to build a website that generates leads

  1. State what you do and who it is for in the first screen.
  2. Give each service its own landing page with one clear call to action.
  3. Keep forms short. Ask only for what you need to follow up.
  4. Add trust signals: reviews, client logos, certificates and real photos.
  5. Connect forms and WhatsApp to your CRM so no lead is missed. Our WhatsApp automation can reply instantly.
  6. Track cost per lead, not just traffic, and test headlines and offers.

Match the website to your business model

Business modelWhat the website must do
B2B servicesBuild credibility with case studies and capture qualified leads
B2C retailHelp people find products and buy easily (see ecommerce development)
Local servicesLocation pages, reviews, booking and click-to-call
SaaSProduct tours, pricing, free trials and sign-up
Start-up (early stage)A focused landing page to test demand, then grow

Design ideas by industry

Healthcare sites need trust, accessibility and appointment booking. Meanwhile, SaaS sites need product tours and clear pricing. Retail needs search, filters and a smooth checkout. Professional services need credentials and case studies. Match the layout, content and calls to action to how your buyers decide.

Plan your business website with Openink Hub

Planning business website development step by step

First, list the people your site must serve: buyers, partners, investors and job seekers. Next, give each group a clear path, so nobody has to hunt for what they need. Then decide what your team must update often, because that shapes the CMS choice, whether WordPress or a headless setup. In addition, plan SEO from day one. For instance, give every service its own page with a clear title and description. After launch, track enquiries, not just traffic. As a result, business website development becomes an investment you can measure. Finally, set a review rhythm, such as every quarter, so the site keeps pace with your business.
